utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, good morning to you. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. For the record, Accused Gvero, General Gvero, is not present because of a medical appointment. He has waived his right to be present for the proceedings today. We've seen it. All the other accused are present. Defence teams, I see that everyone is present. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. I understand there are some preliminaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, Your Honours. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Just one minor preliminary. Back on the 27th of March when we were discussing the time frame for the expert witness that the Defence might call in regards the intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I read this morning that he is coming over this week, later on this week, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour. And at the time we were discussing that on March 27, Mr. Bourgon, on behalf of the Defence, requested that if he did in fact testify around May 23rd, which we now know he will, we would probably ask for an extension to file our motion on the response on the intercepts in total. On April 2nd, Your Honour made an oral ruling at the end of the day stating that we would have -- the Defence would have two weeks after the intercept expert to file our responses. The Defence -- all the Defence teams have discussed this. We all agree and we discussed with Mr. McCloskey this morning, and the Prosecutor has no objection. We are simply asking, Your Honour, if we could have until the 18th to file. It's Monday the 18th since we are not sitting for six working days, and it's not changed. That would essentially mean our response is going to be due in the middle of the week when we are on break. Frankly, Your Honour, probably the end of next week we are going to be scattering like a bevy of quail, and it's going to be very hard for to us complete that mission without that extension. We are all in agreement, even the Prosecution. That's all I want to bring up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Meek. Let me consult with my colleagues, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In problem, the time limit is being extended to the 18th. What day is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It's a Monday, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Judges. Good morning, colleagues. I just wanted to briefly inform the Trial Chamber, Mr. President, the Defence will be filing this morning, before 10.00, a motion for reconsideration of two previous Trial Chamber decisions, and I would just like to inform the Trial Chamber that there is an interim relief sought in this motion. I can expand on it or simply say that there is an interim relief that we believe will require the Court's attention this week. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will look into it, Mr. Bourgon. Any further preliminaries? None. All right. Let's bring in Mr. Trivic. Now, so that I update myself completely, we still have the Gvero Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I have an indication of the time estimate required by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what I was referring to, the Gvero Defence team, you asked for more time to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, yes, more time. I mentioned this at the very close of proceedings on Friday, in fact, and said that we now required a longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I am asking you because going through what I could this morning, it wasn't quite clear in my mind whether you were asking for more or for less; but now it's clear, you're asking for more.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's right. As Your Honour may be aware, Mr. Haynes, really on behalf of all of us defending, addressed the issue of time generally over the next two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thanks a lot. I think, Mr. Thayer, you may proceed. Mr. Trivic, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not Mr. Thayer who is addressing you; it's me. You didn't see me here last week. I am the Presiding Judge. We are going to continue with your testimony today. It's very unlikely that we finish today, and I am not quite sure that we will finish tomorrow, but we'll do our utmost. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you and Your Honours. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We left off on Friday, on 10 July, 1995, you had finished telling us that you had been redirected towards the area of Stupina?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was redirected towards Stupina, or rather, the northwest elevations or mountains relative to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did your combat group, in fact, occupy positions in that area to which you it been directed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It did occupy positions in keeping with the task received that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you, yourself, spend the evening of 10 July back in the command post in Jasenova?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, that brings us to the 11th of July, sir. On that day, did you and your forces advance towards the Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, we continued on the same main axis towards the northwest, or rather, western heights overlooking the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were the Zvornik Brigade forces still your neighbours to the right at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe what your location was when you learned that Srebrenica had, in fact, fallen?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally was located at the first, right, sharp bend overlooking the town of Srebrenica, to the west, to the southwest.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you at some point personally enter the actual town of Srebrenica, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who, if anyone, accompanied you from your combat group?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was with Major Eric, who was in the capacity of commander of the combat group; a communications officer; and some other people that I cannot name. But at any rate, Major Eric and I entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you entered the town, did you encounter General Mladic at some point?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was already in Srebrenica when General Mladic appeared, accompanied by General Zivanovic and General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you describe, please, what you and General Mladic said to each other during that encounter?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to the customary exchange of greetings, I wanted to remind him of the events of two years earlier, on the same day, in the area of Trnovo, when a road was opened up and communication was established with Herzegovina, the way that leads from Sarajevo towards Kalinovik and Foca. Until then, the road had been unusable to us, so we had to travel to Herzegovina via Montenegro. That's what I wanted to remind him of.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall anything else about any exchange that you had with General Mladic while you were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if you can call that a conversation because it was between a subordinate and a superior. He issued the assignments he had to issue. He told me something, "Never mind the history, head for Potocari." And I informed him that I was carrying out the task I had received that morning, and that was the end of the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, again, sir, the task that you had received earlier that day was what?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just before the -- this last answer I told you, my task was to occupy positions on the heights in the western part of Srebrenica, on the heights overlooking Srebrenica, not in the town itself. And he gave me an assignment to protect that side from any surprises, to secure the units located there from any surprise attacks by the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. At this time what I'd like to do is show you a couple of video clips.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we'll probably pick up the audio in a few moments, but for now I'll simply ask you -- we are at 1 minute 42.1 seconds of this video clip. Do you recognise the individual in this frame holding the radio in his right-hand?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's Major Jolovic, also known as Legenda. That it was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there is no sound, and there is no subtitles in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know that, but for the time being, I said nothing because Mr. Thayer said it was coming at some point, and we were only asking the witness to identify the person on that clip. But if we are going to proceed now and not just ask a question on the person who may be appearing or who appears on this clip, we need sound obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we can get by without sound for the next few questions, and hopefully we will pick it up by then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we are looking at a clip at 2 minutes and 00.3 seconds. Do you recognise anyone in this video clip?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This man holding a receiver of a radio device is me, and the person in the foreground I don't recognise. I don't recall him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, do you recall, approximately, or do you recall what date and at what location this piece of footage is being filmed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The recording is probably dated. I suppose it's from a video made in Srebrenica. It's hard to guess. But if it's from that video, then I suppose it's the 11th of July. You know, looking at one insert taken out of context, it could be anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, that's my only question is if looking at this photograph you can recognise where it is or what day it is. I understand that you have difficulty with that at this time. Let's move on, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This I take it is a video or this part at least is a video that was broadcast on some TV media, because I see at the top right-hand corner the logo of one of the stations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we are pausing at 2 minutes 22.8 seconds. Do you recognise the location depicted in this frame?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, I believe this is the road leading to the town of Srebrenica, from the location where I was on the 11th; and since I passed by this road, I think this is the bend on the road that comes just before the descent into Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, is this the bend which you described a few moments ago in your testimony, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a bend a bit further below, from the one where I was. That's where the road starts to meander before descending into Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So the bend that were you describing earlier is a little bit to the north of this position, is that correct, closer to Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This bend is closer to Srebrenica, along the road at least. You know what a serpentine road looks like. Maybe this is more southerly, but it's closer to town than the one where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we are going to broadcast a new clip now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we've paused it at 28 minutes 38.7 seconds. Just briefly, would you describe anyone you recognise in this frame, starting with the individual at the far right of the frame?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gentleman on the right-hand side of this still is Captain Godinic from my combat group. The person greeting -- exchanging greetings with General Mladic is the president of Sokolac municipality, Mr. Milan Tupajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recognise yourself at the far left there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, of course. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recognise, sir, at 28 minutes 46 seconds, the individual at the far right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's General Zivanovic, corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, at 28 minutes 54.5 seconds, do you recognise the individual standing to General Mladic's right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Major Ljubo Eric, commander of the combat group.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And a moment ago, just prior to this frame, there was a woman with a rifle over her shoulder. Can you identify her for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an officer in the organ for moral guidance in the brigade command. Her name was Dana, and I can't remember her family name, but she was with the combat group there on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you say brigade command, you're referring to your brigade, the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, at 29 minutes 22 seconds, do you recognise yourself in the left-hand portion of this frame?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you just describe what you have in your left hand?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't make out. I can't see it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's advance the film then a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Does that help you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a radio set, a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And with your radio set, with whom were you in communication?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose I was communicating with one of my commanding officers, who were occupying positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall if there is a reason why you were using a Motorola in Srebrenica town, as opposed to the phone kit that we saw you using in the prior clip?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that I used a Motorola rarely in combat activities, and you could see it in the earlier still as we were getting into Srebrenica. This was a radio set used by the establishment. At that point in time, I didn't have one, and I suppose I was given it by someone to issue orders to a commanding officer who had a Motorola. I believe it was Major Eric's set that he used to keep in touch with the formation that was engaged in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall, approximately, what time of the day this footage was shot on July 11th?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, and based on what I stated in my documents, it must have been around 800 hours -- 1800 hours. I can't be precise, and I'm sure one can trace the time of the day on the footage itself, on the video, but I believe it was around 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was this the first time you had been in direct contact, direct personal contact, with General Mladic during this operation, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that operation, this was the only personal contact. I had not had any personal contacts with him before that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall any radio communications that you may have had with General Mladic during this operation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been quite a while. I don't recall anything in particular, save for this one point at which General Mladic issued a warning over the radio communications, which was meant for all the units, that NATO aviation fire was imminent. A commanding officer informed me about this, and he was quite surprised to have heard General Mladic over the radio communications. I myself did not have any personal radio communications with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You just referred to some NATO aviation fire. Do you recall actual NATO air strikes that day, 11 July?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After hearing this communication, there were air strikes. The communication took place along the route from the repeater toward Srebrenica. The air strikes took place at an area where there was a clearing, and some combat vehicles were moving along that particular road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall, approximately, what time of the day those air strikes took place?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several hours before my entry into the Srebrenica town. It was the middle of the day. If what we just saw was around 1800 hours, then the air strikes must have taken place around 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, did you spend the night of 11 July at Jasenova?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That brings us to the 12th of July, sir. Can you describe what you did that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, in the morning, I was ordered over a radio communication that I should report to the repeater at Bojna, and I went there. Assignments were issued there by Colonel Vitic [as interpreted], and those were the assignments for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Couple follow-up questions, sir. First, do you recall, approximately, what time of the morning you reported to this location?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At around 9.00 in the morning on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you referred to a TV repeater and this location Bojna. Can you describe, approximately, where this location is in reference to the two bends that you told us about a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This location is on a peak which is normally the location where one places TV repeaters. In relation to the first bend, where I was at the time we were observing and taking up positions, and I'm referring to my unit, the repeater was perhaps a kilometre or two to the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you described a colonel who was issuing orders at this meeting, and it's been translated here as "Vitic." Is that correct or was the colonel's name something else?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Colonel Vicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what position did Colonel Vicic hold, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Drina Corps command, he was the chief of the operations and training or he was one of the operatives there. At any rate, he was working for the operations organ, at the time of the combat activities that ensued when this particular assignment was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And given that Colonel Vicic was issuing orders at this meeting, do you have any recollection, as you sit here today, as to whether General Krstic was actually present for this particular meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'll allow for the possibility that I cannot give you a precise answer. He did not issue any assignments. To the best of my recollection, and I'm not quite certain about it, I recall that Colonel Vicic received the commanders. He greeted us. It is quite possible that he went elsewhere, or rather, I'm referring to Krstic. I do recall that it was Vicic who was the one giving us assignments for that day. I am certain about that bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall any other brigade commanders who were present for this meeting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the last part of the witness's answer is not recorded. At the end of that phrase, the witness said that Vicic, in fact, conveyed tasks issued by another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is correct. But can I suggest that you put your question again and you answer it again, Mr. Trivic? The reason is that the interpreters didn't manage -- or not the interpreter, but we never got it in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you follow that exchange?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Again, at this meeting, you indicated that Colonel Vicic was issuing orders. Do you recall whether General Krstic was present for this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that, to the best of my recollection, I greeted General Krstic that morning, and it is quite possible that he only received the commanders and greeted them and Colonel Vicic passed the assignments on on behalf of the corps commander. He issued them on his behalf, and those were the assignments for that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And before we discuss the specific assignment that you received, sir, do you recall which other brigade commanders were present for this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume that they were because all of us received assignments. I did and so did they. They were supposed to be there, and I believe that they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you have any specific recollection of any specific brigade commander being present for this meeting, in addition to expecting that they would in accordance with standard army discipline?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since all of my attention was directed toward the people who were sitting next to me to my left or to my right, and I mean the adjacent units of Zvornik and Bircani, Colonel Pandurevic and Colonel Andric were there. Since I did not make any notes of that, and more than ten years have passed, it's very difficult for me to say for some people that they were there certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So briefly, sir, what orders did you receive at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For that day, the group that was within my unit and under the command of Major Eric, and I mean the combat group, received the following assignment: From the positions they were occupying at the time, they were supposed to move toward the Jahorina feature via Viagor village. The route they were assigned was the road going from Srebrenica to Milici across Viagor village, and I mean the right side of that road. They were supposed to search the area - that was the term used at the time - to conduct searches for possible enemy units, elements of the 28th Division who were deemed to have headed in that direction or were present along that route.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you in fact, sir, return to your group's position and convey those orders?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Having received my assignment, I went to my unit, my commanding officers, and I conveyed those assignments or I issued these assignments. That was within my competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you receive another order that day, to attend another meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One should distinguish between the gathering that took place in the morning and the meeting that took place that day. The morning gathering of the commanders on the ground had the purpose of issuing assignments for that day on the ground in an area that is clearly visible, where you can show the axes along which the units had to be engaged; whereas, in the afternoon, I received an assignment from General Krstic in the area of Viagor village that I should come to the Bratunac Brigade command post, and I was told that I should go there that evening for a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, sir, did -- were you required to report to this area, Viagor, at which time you received this further order from General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was accompanying the unit as it was carrying out this assignment. As I reached the northeastern slopes of Jahorina, over the communications device, I was told that I should go back to where the first houses of the Viagor village on the edge of the village were, and that there I ought to report to General Krstic, who was waiting for me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just one clarification, sir, you have referred to a feature at Jahorina; and just to be clear, this is not the well-known ski resorts of Jahorina. Is that correct? This is another smaller feature in the area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a peak in this mountainous area between Srebrenica and Milici. If I can be shown a map, one of the features is Jahorina and the other one is Jastrebaca, which is just next to it. I'm not quite sure which of the two lies on the left-hand side and which on the right-hand side. It can be seen on the map. If Jahorina is on the right-hand side, then that's the feature where I took my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we'll break out the maps in a little while, sir. Do you recall whether General Krstic ordered you to be in Bratunac by a particular time for this meeting on July 12th?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that I was supposed to be at the command post of the Bratunac Brigade at 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And from what location did you depart to attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I went to Jasenova and from there on, at any rate, I passed on my way through Srebrenica and Potocari before reaching the command post in -- of the Bratunac Brigade in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, approximately, what time was this that you passed through Potocari, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I was required to be at the destination at 2100 hours, I must have passed through Potocari at least half an hour before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you describe what you saw in Potocari when you passed through?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many people in Potocari, crowds of people. On the road itself, while I wouldn't say that there were crowds of people, but at any rate there were people moving along the road to the left and to the right road side, and one had to pass through that section of the road quite slowly. Military and civilian police officers, several of them, tried to maintain order and make way for the vehicles passing along that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And on this trip, sir, on your way through Potocari, did you see anyone being placed on buses at this time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you described military police being present. How could you tell that they were military police, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the uniforms, equipment, belts, it was typical of the military police. They had belts worn by all the military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, is distinctive about those belts, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that there was something special in the dress of military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right. What time did you arrive in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure it was before 2100 hours because I was not late. I made sure that I was on time, as I had been told, but not -- I didn't come too early.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you describe please what occurred when you arrived at Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. What could have occurred?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters for this meeting that was scheduled that you were ordered to attend?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I went to the operations room to ask where the meeting would be. It was the operations room of the Bratunac Brigade, and I was directed to a room upstairs in that building where the command of the Bratunac Brigade was stationed. So I was directed not to the operations room but to the room where the meeting would be held.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether there were any other brigade commanders present at this time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly, there were some brigade commanders. I did not arrive first or last. Some people were already there. Now, who came before and who came after, I don't know. But there were some people already when I arrived, and the meeting hadn't yet started.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall specifically seeing any of the brigade commanders present at this meeting? Who do you remember seeing?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you about the people I'm sure about: Colonel Pandurevic, in view of the way the meeting went, from that point on, I'm sure that he was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And given your prior testimony about your expectation that other brigade commanders involved in this operation would have been present at certain other meetings, is your expectation the same with respect to the attendance of brigade commanders for this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. That's the military norm. The commander summons, issues assignments, and, therefore, the commander must be present himself, rather than delegate the duty to somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And earlier in your testimony, sir, you referred to the Skelani separate Battalion. Would you expect Colonel Vukotic [sic] to have attended this meeting as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Colonel Vukota. My personal opinion is that, in view of his status in the missions he had been involved in until then, that he was not present. It's possible that I'm mistaken and that he was present. But from the previous engagements of his units, I would say that he wasn't at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber which Drina Corps commanders were present for this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was General Krstic at that meeting, as operations commander; I was there; and I'm certain about Colonel Pandurevic. I'm not -- I can't be sure about the others. It's possible that some people had called the commander up beforehand saying that they were otherwise engaged, that somebody else should be sent in their stead. I'm only sure, therefore, about myself and Colonel Pandurevic. About the others, I can only expect that they should have been there and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether General Zivanovic was present for this meeting, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether any Main Staff officers were there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing any Main Staff officers in Bratunac or Srebrenica when you were there during these few days in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't encounter anyone, either during the meetings or during the activities between the 6th and the 13th. At any rate, it was an operation planned by the Drina Corps, and it was commanded by the operations commander and the command of the Drina Corps. But I didn't run into anyone and I didn't communicate with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall seeing any MUP officers at this meeting or in Bratunac or the Srebrenica area when they -- when you were there for these few days?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, at some point General Mladic arrived during the course of this meeting; but prior to his arrival, can you describe what, if anything, occurred during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before General Mladic arrived, I don't recall anything in particular; although, when I studied the events during the Blagojevic case and in part of my interview, I believe there was a bit of conflict between General Krstic and Blagojevic. After all those contacts, that's something that vaguely sticks in my mind, but I'm not sure I was aware of anything of that kind at the time. I had no communications with the commander, apart from the usual reporting about my unit; and until General Mladic's arrival, there is nothing in my mind that sticks as an extraordinary event. It was all regular activity, business as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What time did General Mladic arrive, and can you describe what happened at the meeting once he did arrive?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He arrived at 10.00 p.m., congratulated us on our successes thus far, greeted us, of course, and gave out an assignment to General Krstic to prepare for the operation that would follow in the area of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what details were provided to you at that time about the Zepa operation, either by General Krstic or General Mladic himself?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the decision followed from the announcement of General Mladic to all of us that the success should be capitalised upon and operations should continue to liberate Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you or any other commander, brigade commander, there have a particular reaction to that order at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Pandurevic was the first to respond, and I supported him. He took the position that the troops that had been engaged in the operation so far should rest and be replaced, but he was overruled. The order came to continue with the same troops in the area of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did Colonel Pandurevic or yourself have any response to being overruled at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you cannot call it a response. It was our need to acquaint our superior officer with the situation within the unit and to try to win him over, to change his decision; however, it didn't work.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, in response to being overruled, did you or Colonel Pandurevic make any suggestions to Generals Krstic or Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not outvoted. It's not right to put it that way. It is the unquestionable right of the commander to make decisions. We tried to suggest that this part of the troops that had been involved in the operations thus far in separating the enclaves and the troops that had been in preparation during those few days should be given a rest, replaced, and prepared for a new mission. So we attempted to bring it to the notice of our superior that he should not use the same troops but it is the privilege of the commander, and that's the way I thought of it, to decide ultimately. And we did not succeed in changing his mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, what, if anything, did you succeed in asking of Generals Krstic and Mladic with respect to your tired troops?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, nothing. Nothing changed. All we could do was accept the mission and go, move to a new area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: During this meeting, sir, or at any time that you recall, did you or Colonel Pandurevic ask General Krstic or General Mladic to address your troops?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When it was all over, we demanded, and I believe Colonel Pandurevic initiated this suggestion, that General Mladic, with all the authority he wielded, address the troops and tell them that what they had been told before was not going to happen, so as to make it more painless for them to accept that they would have to go on in those difficult conditions, high temperatures, shortage of water, fatigue, et cetera, all the problems that plagued the units in the eight days that they had already spent in that area. So it was agreed that before the movement to Zepa, General Mladic would address the troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when did General Mladic agree to do this, sir? When was that agreement to do that forthcoming?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that meeting, it was accepted and it was agreed that this speech would happen on the 13th, before movement to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during this meeting with Generals Mladic and Krstic, did you receive or did you hear any orders issued concerning securing any of the communications or roads in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Among other things, the troops, the units that had been normally deployed in the defence area of the Drina Corps, received the assignment to secure the roads, to guard the roads from Srebrenica towards Vlasenica via Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And which units or brigades would those have been, sir, that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who had those roads in their area of defence. That's the Bratunac Brigade, Milic Brigade, and I don't know which other brigades, but the brigades that normally covered the roads within their zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were these units supposed to execute this task alone or with the assistance of any other forces, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the assignment was issued to operate in cooperation with the forces of the MUP. They were to guard the roads jointly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was there any particular concern that you recall at that time which prompted this order to secure those roads with MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, there was a concern. The forces of the 28th Division had not surrendered their weapons and had not agreed to disarm and surrender; instead, according to our evaluation, which was confirmed later, they headed for the territory of the then-Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina through our area of defence, and it was anybody's guess to what extent they were well or badly organised. In any case, we needed to move our units in that area, units of the brigade, and units of the corps, towards the broader area of Zepa. So it was one of the primary tasks of the commander to give some thought to how the troops should go along such roads, through such an area, where they are at risk of ambush while making sure that all communications and all support work properly. That's why the roads were to be secured as a primary task, when columns of troops are supposed to march on the road, and they are at their most vulnerable at that time, and the same goes for vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall who issued that particular order with respect to securing the roads?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who uttered the words, but it was ultimately the obligation of the operations commander to issue that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that would have been whom, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said I don't remember who uttered the words, but it was incumbent upon General Krstic, as commander of the operation, to stipulate that, to give that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, at some point during this meeting, sir, in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, did you overhear General Mladic in any conversation on the telephone?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What did you hear, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That telephone call took place in connection with procuring vehicles to transport people from Potocari area and procuring the fuel. I think, in fact, I don't think, I heard General Mladic say to whoever he was speaking to on the phone that that was necessary, and he asked that other person to take care of the fuel; whereas, he himself would make sure that vehicles are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And after this meeting, sir, what happened next at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting was over, we left that room and went to dinner. A dinner had been organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is it fair to say, sir, that this dinner was attended solely by Generals Krstic, Mladic, and the brigade commanders, or do you recall anyone else being present for this dinner?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dinner was for the same group of people that attended the meeting before.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And after the dinner, did you return to Jasenova, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After that dinner, I returned to my command post in Jasenova.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you were driven back to your base. Do you recall anything about the drive back to your base that night?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drove back in my own vehicle with my own driver. I don't recall anything in particular. I believe I dozed off in the car. There were no obstacles on the road because of which we had to stop, no incidents that would engrave it in my mind. I just returned to my command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see it's almost 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it is almost 10.30. We'll have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning again, sir. Sir, before we move to the 13th of July, I wanted to ask you a few more questions about this meeting on the evening of the 12th at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters. You testified that the Muslim forces and military-aged men, as far as your intelligence and information were concerned, had not surrendered at Potocari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, before you give your answer, please, for the record, General Gvero is now present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I stated that elements of the 28th Division, or that was our evaluation, did not agree to surrender or disarm. I was talking about elements of it. Probably they were attempting to cross over to the territory under the control of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So their whereabouts were generally unknown, but, as I believe you testified, there were concerns that they would be attempting to move through VRS-held territory in the direction of Tuzla and Kladanj; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, from your intelligence briefings or other information that you had gathered, do you recall, approximately, what the strength estimates were of these Muslim forces that you were concerned might be breaking through to Muslim-held territory?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that point we knew that most of the forces of the 28th Division were involved. That was the intelligence that we had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm not asking you for a specific figure, but what were the estimates, if any, that you were receiving? Were they in the hundreds, the thousands, or the tens of thousands of Muslim forces that might have been trying to break through?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several thousand. That was, I believe, the estimate that was presented at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, at any time during this meeting on the 12th of July at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, was the procedure with respect to any of these prisoners who were likely to be captured discussed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "prisoners"? I don't understand that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Was it ever brought up during this meeting on the evening of the 12th what your forces or any of your fellow brigade forces were supposed to do with any prisoners or any military-aged men or Muslim army members that you captured or who surrendered to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall any discussion at all during this meeting on the 12th regarding what would happen or what the procedure would be in general if any military-aged men were captured or surrendered to VRS forces?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall any mention of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time of this meeting, sir, that separations of military-aged men from their families had taken place during the day on July 12th in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that military-aged men, as well as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Is there something wrong with the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] No, Your Honour. I object to this line of question. The previous one was a leading question, and now my learned colleague is starting to lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm simply asking a question that he may know the answer to or not. I don't believe I'm suggesting any answer to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's not a matter of suggesting an answer or not. It's to make a suggestion that will bring an answer. A leading question does not have to be something that you suggest the answer to the witness. It is suggesting something to the witness that will recall something that he might otherwise recall differently, and this is clearly a leading question. My colleague has been doing that throughout with this witness. We don't say anything, but at some point we have to get down to normal questions and open questions for this witness to give what he knows and what he saw. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I can rephrase, Mr. President, if that makes it easier for everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware whether there had been any separations of Muslim men of any age from their families in Potocari during the day on 12 July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It's still a leading question. He can ask the witness whether he saw some people being separated. He cannot use this suggestion that men were being separated. What did this man see with regard to buses or in Potocari or what were his observations? Those are open questions. But if he asks, Did you see separation, he is suggesting that there were indeed separations. Now, this witness has already answered questions about what he saw and what he did not see in Potocari or other places, and we should stick to that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was not whether he saw separations, at least the last question, whether he was aware, whether there had been any separation of Muslim men of any age from their families in Potocari during the day of the 12th of July, and I see no direct question in there. It's a simple, straightforward question. If he is aware of such separation having taken place on that day, he can tell us; if he is not aware, he is equally competent to say, No, I'm not aware of such happening. It's not a direct question. Let me just consult as well with my colleagues to make sure that I'm on the right track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are all in agreement here. Go ahead. If you wish to read out or repeat your question to the witness, but I can read it out myself actually. Mr. Trivic, you're being asked whether you were aware whether there had been any separation of Muslim men of any age from their families in Potocari during the day of the 12th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, during this meeting, was there any discussion about placing captured or surrendered Muslim men in detention locations in and around Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, there it is. I'd go back about a page or two, and this has been asked two times in a row to this witness. It's been asked and answered, this question has been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you that a similar questions were asked where the discussions, whether this was any plan or not, but this is a more specific question and he can answer it. I mean, go ahead, Mr. Trivic, if you can answer that question, please. And the question is: During this meeting, last meeting that you were referred to, was there any discussion about placing captured or surrendered Muslim men in detention locations in and around Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no discussion about that at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So, sir, did you become aware at any point prior to your departure from that meeting whether or not prisoners were being held close to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters in the Vuk Karadzic engineering school?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If you get the answer "no" to the general question and you then ask a slightly more specific question and you get the answer "no," what's the purpose of asking a further even more specific question? This really is asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I asked whether he became aware at any point prior to his departure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From that meeting, yes. Now, the specifics of the question itself makes it different from the ones that were asked before because it refers to a specific time. Mr. Trivic, we are referring to the point in time which is prior to your departure from that meeting. At that point in time, did you become aware or had you become aware whether or not prisoners were being held close to the Bratunac Brigade headquarters in the Vuk Karadzic engineering school in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already answered that. The only thing I know was discussed was the people who had been routed in the village of Potocari. This was in the context of the procurement of vehicles and fuel, and General Mladic discussed this matter with one of the persons at the meeting, but there was no mention of any prisoners, to use the term you used. In fact, these were not prisoners. These were people who came into the area of the UN base in Potocari of their own will. There was no other mention of -- or rather, I don't know anything else about people, transport, or evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I have just one more question on the 12th before we move to the 13th. You described what you saw as you passed through Potocari close to the end of the day on the 12th, on your way to this meeting in Bratunac. You described, I believe, seeing many people or a crowd of people. Do you recall whether or not you saw any military-aged men in that crowd at that time when you passed through Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that crowd of people, in that multitude of people, there were persons of all ages, of both sexes. There were children and women and men of all ages. That's something I remember. I do remember seeing persons of different ages and both sexes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, did you ever receive any information during this period of time, and I'll expand it to the 13th as well, that there may have been as many as a thousand military-aged men in Potocari? Did you ever receive that information?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't. I can't remember knowing this or hearing about it. To put it simply, I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to the 13th. You testified previously that General Mladic had agreed to address your troops the next day. That would have been this morning, the morning of 13 July. Did he do so, sir; and if so, where did this occur and, approximately, what time of the day?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct that on the morning of the 13th, between 10.00 and 11.00 a.m., he addressed troops in the area where most of the troops were stationed, the combat arms that were assigned to sweep that area. That was in the area of the Jahorina feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just briefly, sir, we don't need to spend too much time on this, what did he tell your troops?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told them what he had previously told us, the commanders. He commended them for their successes and successful performance of their previous missions, and told them that they should carry out their impending mission in the same way. He told them to be proud, and he told them what normally the commander of a Main Staff is expected to tell the troops, to motivate them and to mobilise them to perform the impending tasks regardless of the fatigue or the consequences they felt of the actions they had previously carried out in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was General Krstic also present for this address; and if so, did he issue you with any further orders?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Krstic accompanied General Mladic, of course. He gave more specific assignments relating to the impending march they were to engage in, and he told them of the area to which the unit was to be deployed and by what time this had to be done. To put it shortly, he had to give them the assignment that the unit had to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you told to be somewhere by a particular time, sir; and if so, when to both questions?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we were told by what time we were supposed to deploy the unit to the area of the village of Krivaca. The deadline was 1900 hours on the 13th. By that time, the unit had to be in the area. They were also told the route along which they would march.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I take it you passed those instructions on, and if you took a different route to Krivaca, can you describe what your route was, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assignments resulting from General Krstic's order were specified by me. I told them that they had to march along the route given. I personally went via Srebrenica and Bratunac into that same area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that's the communication that runs through Konjevic Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At this time if we may have P02116 displayed on e-court? It may take a moment or two because it's a map and we'll need to zoom in on a certain portion when it does. Now, if we could zoom as much as possible, if we could scroll up a little bit, little bit further, please, little bit more. And then to the right, please, just a little bit. I'm sorry. Just a little bit down, scroll a little bit down. Okay. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, with Madam Usher's assistance, I'm just going to ask you to circle various locations which you've described in your testimony so far, just so we have a reference later on to these areas that you were talking about. And if you need a couple minutes or couple moments to read the map that we are looking at, please do so. I would ask you first to circle the location marked Jasenova, if you see it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you also see Kiprovo? You also mentioned that location.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You mentioned Bojna?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the village, and the repeater is on this peak here. [Marks] I believe it's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you would, sir, just draw an R next to that circle you just marked repeater?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you can locate Stupina and circle that, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I see on this map that Viogor is marked vertically as a region. To the best that you can recall, can you circle the area at which your meetings you described, I think, a second house in the village of Viogor. Can you just indicate that location with a circle and place a V next to that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is the bend. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, finally, sir, you described a destination of Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We may need to scroll up a little bit unless we are frozen out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think you can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think, if you look carefully, you might be able to see it; and if you can't see the whole thing, can you just circle what's left of the word?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Madam Registrar, can we zoom out a little bit? If you need him to mark Jahorina, you need to finish with this first.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll move on. I think we can identify it from another area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think you also referred to Jastrebaca or something to that effect. If you see that, could you indicate where Jahorina is in respect to that location, that will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, Jahorina, as such, does appear but it's cut right through.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We just missed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You've indicated with brackets a location, sir, in the upper left-hand corner of the map. What is that location, just for the record?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Jahorina, a geographic feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you just place your initials at the bottom right-hand of the map and put today's date, it's the 21st of May, please, and then we can save it.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: 21st of May.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. That will be good enough. We can save it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Usher. Do we have it saved? Great. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That will be all the questions I have for this exhibit, sir. Let's move on. You described taking the route that led you through Bratunac and ultimately along the road that intersects with Konjevic Polje. Did you pass through Potocari again on 13 July?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I passed through Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please describe what you saw on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I observed in Potocari that people were being loaded on to vehicles that were probably to evacuate them to a different location. That is what could be seen in Potocari itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what type of vehicles are you talking about, sir, seeing?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were buses and trucks, trailer trucks as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you see any VRS soldiers there, sir; and if so, what were they doing with respect to this process?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers and members of the MUP, the police, who were keeping things orderly and making sure that people boarded buses and trucks in good order and that they walked in lines towards them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, you've described this previously: Do you recall seeing how the civilians were being grouped at all?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Potocari, on the right-hand side, there were smaller groups about to get into vehicles; and on the left side, left to me, there was a large number of people who were crossing the road to the side where the vehicles were on the right. So groups of people were going towards the vehicles, and policemen and soldiers were directing them towards the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you see any VRS soldiers along the road as you passed through Potocari; and if so, can you describe how they were deployed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the whole length of the road, one could see soldiers standing 100 to 200 metres from each other, not only soldiers but also policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you stop in Bratunac for any reason; and if so, do you recall what time it was when you left Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bratunac, I stopped by the Bratunac Brigade command to inquire where, because the kitchen always worked, where I could eat, and I went to that canteen and had lunch. After that lunch, I headed towards the area of Krivaca to link up with part of the forces that was marching from another direction. I don't know what time it was, but I know that I was there on time; that is, before 1900 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So then, sir, what is your best estimate as to what time you actually left the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe around 1700 hours. I don't know. I cannot tell how much time it took because under those circumstances you had to drive slowly. I can't be sure how much time it took, but I think it was enough time. If I started at 1700 hours, it was quite enough to reach Krivaca by 1900 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And en route to Krivaca, did you see any groups of Muslim prisoners anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I saw a large group of people sitting down on the football pitch in a settlement called Nova Kasaba, on the right-hand side of the road as I was moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall how those prisoners were arranged, if at all, on that football field, in what manner, if at all?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They sat in rows.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you estimate at all, approximately, how many prisoners you saw on that football field as you drove by?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier in my testimony -- it's difficult to give an evaluation knowing the size of the football pitch and the markings on the pitch. It's difficult to evaluate how many people can be seated on 100 square metre. Well, if you manage to estimate that number, you can multiply it by 100. I never tried before to arrive at a number. If you can seat two people on one square metre, then you can possibly calculate how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this, then, sir: Do you recall approximately how full this football field was with prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That entire area was covered with people sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who was guarding them?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to see military policemen, and I believe there were soldiers, conscripts doing their regular military service and who were in training in Nova Kasaba, which had a military police battalion that trained these soldiers; that is, younger soldiers who were in training to become military policemen. I don't know. Maybe there were some senior troops as well, but I remember the younger ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to which unit was this military police battalion attached, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It belonged to the Protection Regiment of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is that also known as the 65th Protection Regiment, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And are you aware of whether or not there is a facility for that military police battalion in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That military police battalion was normally stationed in that area, in that settlement, in the school building, and this site was just outside the settlement. The football pitch was just outside the settlement where those seated people were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And as you passed through this area, sir, was the road secured in any way by way of check-point or any other way; and if so, by whom was it being secured?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we were moving, in keeping with the order on securing the roads, soldiers and policemen guarded the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether any of those soldiers and policemen belonged to any particular unit, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Apart from those that guarded the football pitch, apart from them, I don't know to which unit the others belonged.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during this period of time, in July of 1995, did you know any of the officers within the 65th Protection Regiment or the military police battalion of that regiment personally; and if you did, can you tell the Trial Chamber their names and position?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly knew the regiment commander, Colonel Savcic, and I also knew Major Malinic, who was the commander of that battalion in Nova Kasaba, the battalion that had those young soldiers in training.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So I take it you arrived at Krivaca; and when you did, to whom did you report, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As is customary, I reported to the forward command post of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who was present at that forward command post? To whom did you report when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't report personally that evening on the 13th. I reported through communications. Since the forward command post had already been established, I reported that my unit had arrived in that area, in keeping with the assignment received that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And Krivaca is a general area, sir. Was there a particular location within that area in which this forward command post was located? Did it have a name?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That command post was set up at an elevation that is called Solila, in the area of Krivaca village.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So what was the assignment that you and your combat group received when you arrived in this area?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received my assignment on the morning of the 13th, and I was already familiar with it. That's why I didn't bother to go to the forward command post that evening, because the task of my combat group was to act as backup force for the operations in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were your forces to serve as a reserve force for any particular unit?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when assignments were being given to units, the main axis is normally determined, the auxiliary axis, and backup forces are designated that are ready to act, to support the units engaged in offensive activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was there a particular other combat group or unit for whom your forces were to act as a reserve force; and if so, who was commanding that other unit?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the main axis of offensive activities in the area of Zepa, parts of the Zvornik Brigade were engaged, commanded by Colonel Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did Colonel Pandurevic and his group leave this area of Zepa at some point; and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Pandurevic, with a part of his brigade that was engaged in this assignment, left the area of Zepa to his own area of defence, after two days, I believe, due to certain problems that occurred, security problems that occurred, in the area of defence of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That problem being several thousand men moving through his area; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose these were forces of the 28th Division, and the direction in which they were pulling out, retreating, passed through the area of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when Colonel Pandurevic and his forces left, sir, what did your forces then do?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In keeping with the assignment I had received, I came into the slot of the main forces and continued to carry out that task that had been set.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you describe -- or how would you describe - let me put it this way, sir - the combat activities in which your forces engaged upon moving into that slot left by Colonel Pandurevic's forces?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like any combat activity performed in an unfamiliar area, the movements of units were very cautious, not being aware of the deployment of enemy forces that had organised defence along that route. We didn't know their strength, their position. So we were slowed down by the necessary caution and care that had to be deployed to perform this task with minimal losses or without any losses. That was what characterised the beginning of this operation. It was a difficult terrain with a lot of depressions, serpentine meandering roads, lots of possibility for ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, we'll look at a map in a few moments, but can you just orient us, generally, to the centre of Zepa, where were your positions, north, south, east or west?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't see it being uploaded as yet. I don't see the map being uploaded. Is there a technical problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I haven't asked for the map. I just wanted to ask him if he could orient us before I call for the map in a few moments. I had a few more questions before getting to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know, I may be wrong, but I think the witness was looking at his screen waiting for the map to show up, and so was I actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I apologise for the confusion, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay. It's no problem. I'm just trying to help you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I'll show you a map in a few moments, but can you just tell us the position that is your forces occupied? Were they to the north, south, east, or west of the centre of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that in my preparations to testify in my previous testimony, and in proofing for this testimony, I focused mostly on Srebrenica itself and the surrounding area, so that over the past 12 years, Zepa has simply not been a subject. I did not think about it. I didn't try to remind myself of that, and I cannot do without a map because I haven't been there in a long time. I don't remember the features. I don't remember the settlements, and I cannot tell you anything about what point is where in relation to what else.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, why don't we go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
