utterances.text: Why don't we go straight to the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Why don't we look at the map that we looked at in your proofing, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That is P02123. If we may zoom in just a little bit further, and maybe up just a little bit, please. Okay. And can we zoom just a tad in further, please, and if we could move up? No. Little down just a little bit. Little bit more, please. I'm sorry, other way. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember looking at this map a few days ago? And if you need sometime to orient yourself to certain of the locations you told me about, then please take your time and do so.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this map a couple of days ago during proofing, and I now recall. I'm trying to recall the area and the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall telling me about an area by the name of Borak?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall that we discussed this. It's a feature that lay on the axis of the engagement of my forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you see Borak on this map, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could you please take the pen and just circle that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you described the location of Solila earlier. Do you see that on this map?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'd just ask you to please put your initials in the lower right-hand corner and today's date, 21 May.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We can save it and we will be done with this map.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher. I think we are done.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did there come a time when your forces were able to break through that area near Borak?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in the days just prior to breaking through, do you recall whether combat or your attack or advance was suspended for any reason; and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Casting my mind back to the few notes I have on this, I believe it was on the 24th of July that this combat group that was part of my unit managed to cross the bed of a river that had gone dry, and this was a frequent occurrence in the summer time. They managed to pull through to the other side immediately below the settlement of Borak, which meant a great deal to the unit because the resistance mounted by the defenders had weakened and conditions were in place for Borak to be defended. My unit stayed there for several days, maintaining the defences there. Because of the lie of the terrain, it was very difficult to go round the unit and approach the feature. On the 24th, they approached the feature and later on the conditions were much more favourable for their further advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And prior to this date, the 24th of July, do you recall whether your advance or your attack was suspended for any reason?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially, once the Zvornik Brigade had opened up the lines, on the first day of engagement while my combat group was in the reserve, it could be concluded in military terms that the offensive activities had been running as per plan, so to speak, or as one would expect. A unit which is engaged in a normal way to slowly advance bit by bit. This lasted several days, at the end of which the forces were able to come out into the area where the settlement of Borak was located. Since those positions overlooked the entire area, it was very difficult to approach the positions without being noticed by everyone. I don't think even a bird could have flown over the area without being noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps I wasn't clear, sir. Were you or your forces ordered at any point to cease your fire during this period of time prior to breaking through on the 24th; and if so, do you recall why?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a more specific question now. On the 19th of July, it was set for the first time that negotiations were entered into, that it was signed that hostilities should cease. As of the 19th onwards, the developments were such that showed that not everything had been observed that had previously been agreed to, and that's why the orders varied.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, when you received the information that not everything had been observed that had previously been agreed to, what did your orders consist in at that point?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally was not told or been informed about what had been observed or had not. We were told that hostilities should cease. However, after a certain period of time, I don't know if it was just a day or ten hours or something like that, it was my personal conclusion that probably due to the fact that the agreement had not been observed, we were told that activities should be launched again as of tomorrow. I, however, was not being informed about the course of the negotiations. On the 19th, we were told that we should cease all activities because a truce had been signed, or rather, not -- it had not been signed; it had been agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At some point after breaking through at Borak, did you personally enter the centre of Zepa; and if so, would you describe what you saw, both en route and when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On one of those days when the hostilities had been suspended, I and some of my commanding officers went to Zepa to see what the settlement was like. Zepa had been discussed a great deal and I wanted to see whether it was a proper town, as I had never been there. On my way, I passed an armoured APC of the UN that had been on the road side, and I saw that General Mladic was involved in discussions about the APC being able to return to travel along the route. We did not dwell there. We were simply waved at my someone telling us to move ahead. In the section of the road where we came out of a wooded area on to a road leading to Zepa, and I suppose Rogatica, we were pulled over. There was a column of buses escorted by UN forces, and I believe there was also the Red Cross and perhaps someone else. This column was transporting the population from the Zepa area, and we were not allowed to resume our trip along the road until the column had fully passed us by. After that, I went to see Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did you observe when you were in the centre of Zepa, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't observe anything in particular. I merely concluded that it was a small settlement in the Zepa valley. There were several houses that were a bit bigger. I don't know whether they were stores or shops or something like that. There was a river, Zepa river, that made a curve there. On that spot, I came across several men, and I mean VRS soldiers, who I exchanged a few words with and went back to join my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And while you were in the centre of Zepa, sir, did you observe any civilians being loaded on to buses at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't go to the centre of Zepa. I was on the edge of the settlement, next to the river where there was a river crossing. I observed the settlement from there. I didn't go to the centre or observe anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you just mentioned seeing General Mladic in the Zepa area. Do you recall seeing any other Main Staff officers in the Zepa area while were you there during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anyone. As for General Mladic, I saw him on my way from my command post along the road, which was actually a forest trail, where he happened to be helping to organise this UN APC that had skidded off the road, helping to organise it to go back along its route.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall being in Solila to discuss with General Krstic a health or sanitation issue that was affecting some of your men?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was with General Krstic. This conversation took part after the first truce was agreed upon, at the time when there were no combat activities. I discussed this issue with him. Whether it was at Solila or not, I believe based on my notes that this command post had already been relocated from Solila elsewhere. I know that now you'll tell me that I mentioned Solila in our conversation during proofing; but after that, I consulted my notes and Solila was no longer the command post at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So, approximately, how long would you estimate you had been on the ground in the Zepa area at this time when you met General Krstic about your men, about the condition of your men?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for a fact that it took place after the truce had been agreed upon because I wouldn't be able to discuss the rotation of my troops whilst the combat activities were going on. It was after the 19th, some five or six days later. Once the truce was signed, I decided to ask for replacements.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, putting aside, as you mentioned, what you may have told me during a proofing session, what is your recollection as to the location of where this meeting with General Krstic took place, as you sit here today?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Flipping through my notes, I recalled that it was in an informal meeting that I asked for in order to be able to tell him this. I wanted to ask him -- now, as for my request to be able to relieve my troops, I can't tell you where this was, where this took place. I know that there were no communications officers accompanying him that would lead me to conclude that this took place at a command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, you just testified a few moments ago that your recollection now is that Solila was no longer the command post. At that time, where was the command post for this operation, sir, if it wasn't at Solila at this time?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the area of Godjenje village. That what was my command post. In the immediate vicinity of my command post, there was the Drina Corps IKM. Now, I don't know of -- as of which date General Krstic -- but I know that at that time, I would be able to have these discussions there about these matters that were of concern to me. This may have been at the Godjenje. That would be the general area of Godjenje, because we had tents in a clearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So do I understand you correctly, sir, then to be testifying that it's your recollection that the Drina Corps command post was moved sometime on or after 19 July to this area of Godjenje?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would go to Godjenje to receive my assignments. There was an area where tents were set up and other equipment that normally follows a commander, that enables him to command the activities taking place. Those were the activities we had at the time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And without breaking out the map again, sir, can you describe, approximately, where this new Drina Corps forward command post was located, let's say, in relation to Borak? Was it to the south of Solila? Just orient us, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. That was to the south of Solila, about five to six kilometres, in the general area of Godjenje village.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, during this meeting with General Krstic, were any Main Staff officers present?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked to see General Krstic, and we met on that date, the 20th or the 21st, I don't know exactly. With him, I met General Gvero as well. Where this was, I don't know. I can't recall. It did not happen at the command post. I don't know. I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, can you describe what, if anything, happened during this meeting, and General Gvero's participation, if any, in this meeting, wherever it may have occurred?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't the meeting. It was me asking to have a word with him, and he said that I should come over. We met in the presence of General Gvero, and I asked General Gvero to tell General Krstic that I be allowed to replace some of my troops who had been plagued by some health problems. A physician, who was there with me as part of the command structure of the combat group, was of the opinion that most of the troops had to be replaced because they had scabies or other health problems that made it impossible for them to properly perform their assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that we are nearing the break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This might be a good place to take the break, if we might.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. One moment, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, it's as if Judge Prost and myself were engaged in telepathy. I was informed that on paper you had indicated two hours, but I was informed that on Friday you suggested that one hour should be enough. We've been three hours already at it plus what happened on Friday. So where do we stand? How much longer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe I have about half an hour left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we do grant you the half an hour, it stands to reason then that the Defence teams may wish to reorganise a little bit their estimated time. Anyway, we'll talk about it when we leave the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer. Our suggestion to you is to accelerate as much as you can your examination-in-chief so that we can move to the cross-examination, also because I understand that there is -- or we may encounter a problem with the next witness if we don't finish his testimony by Thursday. And that's a visa problem, nothing else. But we need to know also from you or from Mr. McCloskey or whoever will be dealing with the Defence expert how much time you require now as of now for his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I may be able to shed some light on that. We've estimated, approximately, a day for cross-examination. Of course, that's an estimate, but we didn't think it was hopefully going to take much longer than that. I consulted with my friends as to estimated time on direct, and I think it's, approximately, the same. That's why we've scheduled two days for the intercept expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the Defence, I have four hours ten minutes here, which is more than a day. If you were to take an entire day, that means he won't finish on Thursday, which means we can't even discuss an extension of his visa. Because it's a single entry visa, he'll have to go back to where he comes from and then get another visa, and I don't like to hassle or create hassle for people especially witnesses who take their time to come and give evidence here. So let's try and finish, and I'm saying this because if the Defence takes six hours in cross-examining this witness, then we are definitely off the mark. We won't be able to finish the expert by Thursday, so let's move, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll do that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall attending a lunch sometime during the period in which were you deployed to Zepa in -- at the Jela restaurant?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall I was invited. In fact, I was ordered to attend a luncheon organised on the occasion of the announcement that General Krstic became corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was this also an occasion to mark the retirement of General Zivanovic, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the luncheon that was in honour of both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who was present at this luncheon, sir, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander of the Main Staff; the chief of Main Staff, General Milovanovic; and ex officio, General Gvero.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall if anybody arrived by helicopter, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Milovanovic certainly came by helicopter because I believe we said hello or goodbye after that luncheon as he was walking towards the helipad. If anyone else was with him in the helicopter, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there was a mistake in the transcript, but it was corrected just as I was about to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Fauveau. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, lastly, sir, I want to ask you discuss a couple of questions about two entries in your diary. At this time, if you still have it with you, sir - and I've also been asked by one of my friends across the aisle to make sure that you have it available for your testimony - it may be easier for you to refer to that original diary, which we furnished to my friends. Feel free to take it out now, sir, if you need to consult with it. We didn't have time to look at this document during our proofing. We ran out of time but I want to ask you about one entry which was illegible, and I want to see if you can make some sense of it. It's at page 6 of the English translation, and that's ERN 0608-5856 of the original B/C/S. It's the portion where you're recording your dinner with General Mladic at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, and it appears that you're recording the order to continue to Zepa and what General Mladic said to you and your fellow brigade commanders at the time. I can show you a photocopy of the page if you need to, to help locate it in your diary, with the assistance of Madam Usher. Have you found it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to compare the text maybe. Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the line that I couldn't read, sir, and I just want to ask you: What you have written here, can you just read from the portion that begins that General Mladic came at 2200 hours? For the record this is 2D00125. Can you just read aloud the entry from your diary, beginning at that point and take it down to the last line on that entry. That's the portion that's illegible.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I start?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At 2200 hours, General Mladic arrives. "First note," or rather, "bullet point. After congratulations and greetings, regardless of the fact that Vinko Pandurevic and I told him that troops need rest, he orders: Tomorrow, by 800 hours, General Krstic is to prepare an order for the liberation of Zepa. Readiness, 14th July in the morning. Time allowed, two days for the liberation of Zepa enclave. This moment of confusion both within the international community and on the enemy's side should be taken advantage of."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, sir. That clarifies the illegible portion in the English translation. The second entry I want to ask you about is at page 1 of the English translation, and that is ERN 0608-5836 of the original. Do you recall an entry made on the 16th of July with the heading of "Major General Krstic" and then four numbered paragraphs? If you can locate that in the original, I can show you the photocopy if that helps you locate it in your diary, and that's page 9 of the B/C/S in e-court, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You've got the four numbered paragraphs, 1, 2, 3, 4. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you just read the first entry, please? I just want to ask you one question about it and we'll be done.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The decision of the Supreme Commander of the VRS is that the eastern part of Republika Srpska must be liberated from Turks."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was your understanding of this statement by General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a soldier, whatever else may be true, I understood the task to liberate Zepa as a task to free that territory from the troops of the BH army that attacked from that area the army of Republika Srpska. So as a soldier, I always understood such tasks as assignments to liberate an area from the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Now, who is going first from the Defence teams? Mr. Krgovic for General Gvero.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I have a few questions about the last subject you've discussed, so I won't follow the chronological order. In your examination-in-chief, you mentioned a brief discussion that you had with General Gvero and General Krstic regarding the health problems afflicting your troops. You also mentioned that you attended that luncheon to celebrate the retirement of General Zivanovic. Was General Krstic there as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That celebration was on the 12th of July in Jela restaurant, just after the cease-fire was signed?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 20th, not the 12th of July. I don't remember the date but the cease-fire agreement was signed later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, the cease-fire was agreed, it hadn't been signed yet?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Agreed, that's what we were told.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This brief conversation you had with Gvero and Krstic, could it have happened during that luncheon at Jela restaurant?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may be mistaken after such a long time. I simply didn't think about that during the Zepa operation until this day. I can't be sure where it took place, but I know I took the opportunity to talk to General Gvero whom I met only once during that operation, because in view of his position, I thought he might be able to suggest to General Krstic that it would be a good idea to approve the replacement of one part of the troops. I don't know what he passed on to Krstic; but in the event, the approval was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: During the operation Zepa, therefore, you saw General Gvero only once?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and then I talked to him on only one occasion. I said a moment ago that I cannot be sure where it happened and when.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you can't rule out the possibility that it was during this celebration in honour of General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a possibility because we were able to talk to each other outside the restaurant, in front of the restaurant. So it could have been then and there, but I can't be sure. The other possibility was the location I mentioned before, Solila, or maybe it was that restaurant. In any case, it was outdoors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Since you saw General Gvero only once, then it must have been there. I put it to you that it was there. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll stand by what I already said. It's a possibility. It could have been right outside that restaurant. Let me just try to explain this. I had only one contact with General Gvero. It was when I asked him for his support in getting my troops replaced, refreshed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago the attendees of that luncheon. You said General Gvero was there ex officio. Now, knowing the position of General Gvero, he was in charge of protocol. He was in charge of organising such celebrations and that was why he was there. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's ex officio, in view of his position, his responsibilities, and it was his duty to have that organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And as the organiser, he would welcome all those present and explain the protocol of it?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that, beforehand, this protocol was presented to somebody as a suggestion and had to be approved. Later on we all complied with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, I'll take you back to the beginning of your testimony and the questions you answered for Mr. Thayer in chief. They have to do with your arrival in Srebrenica area. You said at the beginning that you received orders to come to Srebrenica area from the corps command. The Romanija Brigade was within the corps, right, the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Srebrenica operation and Zepa operation were both operations of the Drina Corps; planned, organised, and carried out by the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That operation was led and commanded by the Drina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived there, were you briefed about the enemy? Was that part of the briefing and preparations?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What were you told? What forces were you facing in Srebrenica area? How many soldiers and policemen were under arms? What kind of information did you have prior to the beginning of the operation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Friday, last Friday, I said a few words about that. We followed the usual procedure; wherein, prior to commencing a task, especially involving units that do not originate from that area, who are unfamiliar with the area, a briefing is indispensable. They have to be given an evaluation of the enemy, the armed forces they are facing, the level of their equipment and strength, and their deployment on features on which they had organised the defence of that area. That was done at Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What exactly were you told? What was the strength of the enemy? How many soldiers and policemen were engaged against you in the Srebrenica operation on the enemy side?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The evaluation said around 10.000 armed people in the protected area. The very name of the unit indicates that number and the name was 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of information did you have about their level of equipment, their weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the intelligence provided by units that had contact with them and the fighting thus far, we were aware that they had not only infantry weapons but weapons that required to be manned by crews, primarily, but not only anti-aircraft guns, machine-guns, some other weapons that were classified as collective ordnance, that requires several operators.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the witness 4D73?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a document that I am not sure you have seen before. It's an analysis of the staff by a branch of service of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Krgovic and Mr. Thayer, this document it's being confirmed to me is under seal. So we can, of course, go into private session and deal with it in private session, or do not broadcast whilst this document is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's better not to broadcast it because I'm not going to go through names on that list, but I'll ask instead general questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Subject to further rulings, for the time being, this document, once it shows up on our screen, our monitor, is not to be broadcast. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Look at page 1. Look at the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown page 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This column that begins with "ARJ, PVO", what is the purpose of that unit?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see that it's an artillery rocket unit of air defence, anti-aircraft defence, and we see the names of the men who were involved in that unit and their duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the weapons they manned?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the equipment they operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the combat operations around Srebrenica and Zepa, did you come under fire from some such weaponry?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the second day of operations; namely, the 10th, before our forces were on the move, my combat group came under anti-aircraft gun and anti-aircraft machine-gun fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Since such weaponry existed and was used in the days of the operation Srebrenica, was it safe to fly helicopters in the Srebrenica and Zepa areas?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusion is that it was not safe, in view of the weapons they had. If you're referring to the flights of helicopters of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: My question was a general one. Was it expected that such weapons would be used to engage any such aircraft in the area?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Flying was unsafe in view of the weapons that were available. It was far from safe to fly over that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, are you aware of the existence of a plan, on the part of some of the UNPROFOR officials, to use helicopter flights around Srebrenica to provoke the VRS soldiers into opening fire at helicopters which would then be used as an excuse for bombing the VRS forces?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Having examined some documents and statements by certain members of the UN forces, I am aware that this was being contemplated as an idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was the proponent of such an idea?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please allow a short pause between question and answer so that the interpreters will be able to catch up with you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. One of the proponents of the idea and the person who was in favour of provoking the VRS fire against the aircraft involved in the distribution of the humanitarian aid to the area was the UN forces commander, Mr. Rupert Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, I will now take you back to the time when you were being received -- when you were being given assignments. When you arrived in the Srebrenica area, in the early days when you were supposed to separate the enclaves, were you given any instructions as to how to treat UN personnel and civilians?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were given assignments to act against members of the 28th Division, and we were told that in doing so we were supposed to avoid any conflicts with the UN personnel at their check-points along the axis of engagement of our units. We were told that the objective of the operations was not the town of Srebrenica itself or the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did your units comply with the order you received?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only natural that one had to comply and act in keeping with the order issued by the commander of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In determining your targets, did you have intelligence and reconnaissance information to the effect where there were enemy forces deployed and where possibly there could have been civilians, too? Did you take that into consideration whilst guiding your fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the date of my arrival in Srebrenica, we were told what possibly the disposition of the units of the 28th Division was. I used such intelligence to guide the movement of my troops by way of invasive reconnaissance and detection of targets. This was in fact done, particularly on the 9th, in the early days of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What information did you have concerning the conduct of the units that were immediately adjacent to you? General Pandurevic's and Colonel Andric's units that were on your left and on your right, did they behave in the same way or did they in any way depart from standard procedure?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything in particular. I only knew, on the basis of the information I had, as to the units to my left and to my right, that they had come across two units of the 28th Division that were better organised in the areas where they engaged their forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At some point, you reached the initial positions that were defined in your order; and, subsequently, you received orders to advance, on the 9th?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of orders did you receive at that point? Were these the orders to seize Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which date you have in mind, but on the 10th I received orders to redirect my forces to -- more to the east, to the western slopes of the heights that lie to the west of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown P33? Could we see the lower part of it, please? That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, on the 9th of July, this document was sent to the Drina Corps. It talks about the way one should proceed in that area. Please look at the second paragraph, which starts with, "The president of the republic is satisfied." This deals with the full demilitarisation of the Srebrenica enclave. Was this in keeping with the order you received?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The second part of it deals with the full protection of members of UNPROFOR and Muslim civilian population?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This, too, was in keeping with the requests put forth by the president of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this latter part, which orders you to provide maximum security and safety to UNPROFOR members, Muslim civilian population, and to refrain from engaging civilian targets?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was a standing assignment, and this was the sort of orders one would receive before commencing an operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you abide by these instructions in combat?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, your neighbours and adjacent units and other units, what was their combat like?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that they also abided -- they also complied with the orders they received from their superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the examination-in-chief, you mentioned that you went through the area of -- the village of Slapovici, and that it was from that side that you entered Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went into this area where there was a settlement of refugees, Slapovic. There were -- there was prefabricated housing there, housing I suppose refugees from different parts of the country who had been living there until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 6D22?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can we see the top of the document?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is an interim combat report of the Drina Corps dated the 9th of July 1995. Please look closely at item 4 of the combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. Could we scroll down?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This report reads that "UNPROFOR at the check-points at the villages of Slapovici and Bocija surrendered to our forces complete with weaponry and equipment and sought our protection." And what is meant here is that they sought protection from the VRS. You said that you passed through Slapovici village. Did you come across any UNPROFOR forces in that period?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I came across a crew of an armoured APC. As they saw us, they came out of the APC and they were very frightened. We communicated to the extent we were able to. I took them, together with my escorts, to the IKM at Jasenova.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you threaten them, mistreat them? How did you, in fact, treat them?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I didn't threaten them. A commanding officer of mine went along the road across Zeleni Jadar to Jasenova together with their driver; whereas, I along with their commander, and I believe there were two more of them, went through the -- through the disposition of my forces all the way to Jasenova where we had a lunch together. They had a beer. I reported on this. That was where our conversation ended and the corps command took them over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you why they were frightened and why they surrendered themselves to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they said that they were afraid of the forces of the 28th Division using them as human shields, and that for that reason they set out toward the VRS forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The combat report you have in front of you, does it reflect the events on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as this episode with UNPROFOR is concerned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, you said that at some point on the 11th, you entered the town of Srebrenica. Before the events of the 11th and the 10th, did your units open fire, or rather, did the town of Srebrenica suffer at the hands of your forces, and did you hear of any other units firing upon the town of Srebrenica on the 10th and the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My unit definitely did not fire upon the town of Srebrenica. The activities of my unit were exclusively focused on the detection of firing positions that had fired upon our units. I did not observe, notice, or hear of any other units firing upon the settlement itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, during the operation in Srebrenica, was heavy artillery used in the course of the operation itself?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in a position to use that fire, and I suppose that this was due to the fact that there had been no planned combat activities for larger calibre weaponry, meaning artillery; rather, we had formed our formations in such a way that we would have small artillery pieces; namely, mortars, so that we could open our way for advancing. I don't think any other units used such artillery fire because we had not even been assigned any such artillery units from which we could seek any such support.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you entered the town, did you observe, out in the street, on the house fronts, any damage inflicted by artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One could not see any such visible damage in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to walk around the centre of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in that part of town that I was, in fact, when the Staff Commander and corps commander came up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the second day, on the 12th, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you observe any damage from shells on the hospital building?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO TRIVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I'm going to stop you here and, again, once more ask you to kindly get together, Mr. Thayer, kindly get together with the Defence teams, to establish a realistic estimate of how long this witness will be testifying tomorrow. From what I see, he's not going to finish tomorrow. If that is the case, you either need to coordinate, together with the Defence, with the Victims and Witness section, to see if possibly one could find a way of extending this gentleman's visa to at least Tuesday of next week. I know it's difficult, but I would like to avoid his having to go back and come again, if we can. Please get together and let us know first thing tomorrow afternoon when we will be resuming. Mr. Trivic, we are going to adjourn now. We'll continue -- yes, Mr. Trivic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to inform you of the following: On the 26th, I have some commitments back in Republika Srpska. I did not expect things to unfold this way, but I would appeal to you to honour this commitment of mine that I have and to make it possible for me to be in Banja Luka on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't see any problems there, Mr. Trivic. The only problem relates to another witness, not to you. You'll definitely be finished if not tomorrow the day after and then you'll be free to go. So tomorrow we'll continue at 2.15 in the afternoon. In the meantime, Mr. Trivic, you're not to discuss with anyone or allow anyone to discuss with you the subject matter of your testimony. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, everybody, and we'll meet -- yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President I just have one item to bring to the Court's attention. We may have identified an individual who we would like to be present in the courtroom to assist the Prosecution during the testimony of the Defence witness, and we would ask the Court's permission to permit to us have that individual present in that role. We haven't lined him up for sure, but we wanted to bring that to the Court's attention now so that we can put things in play.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sure the Defence teams will think about that and respond tomorrow first thing when we start the sitting again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My understanding is we've gotten agreement from Defence counsel on that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then there shouldn't be -- don't expect any problems from our side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 22nd day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
